resources.string: Bulwark can\'t recover lost files, and we are not responsible for lost data.
No internet permission. Check it yourself in Settings → Apps → Bulwark → Permissions.
Your files, locked on your phone. No accounts, no internet, no ads, no tracking. Ever.
Everything is encrypted on this phone
Your files, their names and your folders are encrypted before they are stored. Only your password or recovery key can open them.
The app has no internet permission at all, so nothing can leave your phone unless you export it yourself.
Not even us. If you lose your password and your recovery key, your files are gone for good. That is what keeps them private.
Scroll to the end to continue.
I have read and agree to the Terms of Service
I understand Bulwark cannot recover my files if I lose my password and all recovery methods
This password is the master key to your vault. Use something long that you will remember, or let Bulwark generate a passphrase.
Write this passphrase down somewhere safe before you continue.
Write your password down somewhere safe. Nobody, including us, can reset it.
Check no one can see your screen when you show a password.
Make it longer: 4 or more random words, or 14+ mixed characters.
This is one of the most common passwords. Choose something else.
Sequences like 1234 or abcd are easy to guess.
Add length, words or a mix of characters.
You unlocked with your recovery key. Choose a new password now; your recovery key keeps working.
Choose a new password. The old one stops working immediately. Your files are not re-encrypted, so this is quick.
Choose how you could get back into your vault. Everything stays offline.
24 words you write down and keep safe. They unlock your vault if you forget your password.
If you forget your password, your files are gone for good.
A printable recovery sheet, split recovery and hardware security keys arrive in a later update.
Write these 24 words down, in order, on paper. Keep them somewhere safe and private.
Anyone with these words can open your vault. Don\'t photograph them or store them on this phone.
Copying is turned off on this screen on purpose.
Type these words from your recovery key to make sure you wrote them down correctly.
Those words don\'t match. Check your paper or view the words again.
Without a recovery method, forgetting your password means your files are permanently lost. You can add a recovery key later in Settings.
I understand my files cannot be recovered
Securing your vault. This takes a few seconds while Bulwark tunes its protection to this phone.
Bulwark couldn\'t finish securing the vault. Nothing was saved. Please try again.
This vault couldn\'t be opened because its data is damaged.
This phone\'s security key for the vault is missing, so the vault on this phone can\'t be opened.
Bulwark locks itself when you leave the app, turn off the screen, or stop using it.
Type your 24 recovery words in order. The first four letters of each word are enough.
These words are valid but don\'t unlock this vault.
After unlocking you\'ll choose a new password.
Tap Import to add files. They are encrypted as they come in.
If you forget your password, your files are gone.
This import needs about %1$s free (including safety room), but only %2$s is free. Free up space and try again.
Your battery is at %1$d%%. Plug in your phone before starting a large import.

Plug your phone in and keep Bulwark open until it finishes. Don\'t restart your phone or uninstall Bulwark during the import. Your originals will not be touched. Keep your own copy of these files until you\'ve confirmed they\'re in Bulwark.
Your battery is at %1$d%% and not charging. Plugging in is strongly recommended.
Keep Bulwark open. Locking the vault stops the import safely.
Your originals were not changed. Delete them yourself once you\'ve checked the files in Bulwark.
The exported copy is not encrypted and leaves Bulwark\'s protection. Other apps on your phone may be able to read it.
Export failed. No partial copy was left behind.
No preview for this file type yet
You can export a decrypted copy to open it in another app.
It failed Bulwark\'s integrity check, so it was not opened. It may have been changed or corrupted on the phone\'s storage.
Items in the trash are permanently deleted after 30 days.
\"%1$s\" will be permanently deleted. Nobody can recover it.
Creates new words; the old ones stop working at once
Your recovery words will stop working. If you then forget your password, your files are gone.
Not set: forgetting your password means losing your files
Software only (this phone has no secure key hardware)
Passed: Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305 streaming, keyslots and recovery words checked in %1$d ms.
Uninstalling Bulwark deletes your vault on this phone. Encrypted backups arrive in a later update; until then, keep your own copies of important files.
Biometrics, auto-lock, break-in protection, screen privacy
Every setting starts at its most private choice. Making Bulwark less strict asks for your password first.
Enter your vault password to make this change.
Off. When on, a fresh fingerprint or face match is needed every time; your biometric data never leaves the phone\'s secure hardware.
On. Your password is still required after a restart and when the time below runs out.
This phone has no strong fingerprint or face sensor that Bulwark can use.
Add a fingerprint or face in your phone\'s settings first.
Confirm to turn on biometric unlock
Biometric unlock couldn\'t be turned on. Please try again.
Your phone\'s fingerprints or faces changed, so biometric unlock was switched off. Use your password, then turn it back on in Settings if you want it.
%1$s, and always after the phone restarts
Lock when the screen turns off
Recommended. Locks even within the time above.
Always on: after 5 wrong tries, waits grow from 30 seconds to 1 hour.
After you unlock, see how many wrong passwords were tried while it was locked.
Block screenshots and hide in recent apps
Also blocks screen recording and casting.
Screenshots, screen recordings and the recent-apps preview could then show your files, and other apps could capture them.
Stops someone with your unlocked phone from taking decrypted copies.
Keep items in the trash for
Permanently destroys the vault and its keys on this phone.
Every file in this vault and its keys on this phone will be destroyed immediately. Nobody can undo this.
If that wasn\'t you, someone may have tried to open your vault. Consider changing your password.
